messages.author: 94866edf3707c5ee
messages.subject: 18.07.12 and subsequent broken on Fedora 28
parts:
Running the code from the Scaling IGMRF-models in R-INLA tutorial fails for all releases after 17.06.20 that I've tried on Fedora 28 with R 3.5.1, certainly for stable 18.07.12, but also for most recent testing. Code:

library(INLA)
data(Munich)
g = system.file("demodata/munich.graph", package="INLA")
hyper.prec = list(prec = list(param = c(1, 0.01)))
formula = rent ~
    f(location, model = "besag", graph = g, initial = 1, hyper = hyper.prec) +
    f(year, model = "rw2", values = seq(1918,2001), hyper = hyper.prec) +
    f(floor.size, model = "rw2", hyper = hyper.prec) +
    Gute.Wohnlage + Beste.Wohnlage + Keine.Wwv + Keine.Zh +
    Kein.Badkach  + Besond.Bad + Gehobene.Kueche +
    zim1 + zim2 + zim3 + zim4 + zim5 + zim6 -1
mod = inla(formula, data = Munich)

Have written to help email. Now trying on Windows 18.07.12 stable - it succeeds there, suggesting that the problem is for source install with install.packages(), update.packages() and R CMD INSTALL on Fedora 28 and possibly other Linux systems.

thanks. I'm running Fedora28 myself, and I have no issues. the binary
is buildt on Ubuntu1604.

I just wonder if this is due to the version 0.3.... of openblas, which
I cannot get to work with the pardiso library, so I have kept back the
update and run with version 0.2.20.

can you check by forcing the 0.2... version of openblas to be loaded,
like copying libopenblas into the 'first' directory,

I would do

cd ~/R/x86_64-redhat-linux-gnu-library/3.5/INLA/bin/linux/64bit

$ cp libopenblaso.so.0 first/

-rw-------. 1 hrue hrue 0 May 12 2016 dummy
